title: Simplified protocol for Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of the liverwort Marchantia polymorpha, includes protocols for spore sterilisation
author: Suvi Honkanen

steps_raw.instruction: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of Marchantia polymorpha, includes protocols for spore sterilisation

By Suvi Honkanen and Victor A. S. Jones. Modified from Ishizaki et al. Plant Cell Physiol. 2008 Jul;49(7):1084-91. doi: 10.1093/pcp/pcn085. Developed at the Dolan lab (The University of Oxford) and at the Small lab (The University of Western Australia).

For spore transformation either collect intact sporangiums with extended stalk into 500ul sterile dH2O in Eppendorf tube, or if all the sporangiums are burst or you are going to dry the spores to be used later collect them in an eppendorf tube without water.

Collect 2-7 sporangiums per Eppendorf. Dry them in an open eppendorf tube with a Sun Cap Closure filter on top (or a piece of micropore tape) for 10 days in an air-tight box containing silica gel, and then store in -80°C for up to five years. Freeze the spores prior to sterilisation even if using right away after drying, freezing reduces contamination.
NOTE: Remember to check that your silica gel is not saturated with moisture, the colour of the gel grains is indicative of the level of saturation (silica gel can be dried at a 50°C oven if needed).
Collect archegoniophores with yellow mature sporangiums and place in a petri dish. Place wet tissue at the thallus end of the stalk to keep the archegoniophore alive and maturing.

Sporangiums in a single archegoniophore will be in different stages, it is possible to leave the archegoniophores to mature in the petri dish either on the bench (mature within hours or days) or in 4°C (mature in days or weeks) to collect more intact sporangiums per archegoniophore.
Spore sterilisation using NaDCC
Sterilisation of dried spores stored in the freezer
Prepare sterilisation solution: 1% NaDCC.

Take the spores from the freezer and let thaw until at room temperature. Add 500 ul 0.1% NaDCC (450ul sterile dH2O and 50ul 1% NaDCC). Resuspend the spores by vortexing and pressing the spore clumps against the side of the tube with a pipette tip. It is important to resuspend well to avoid contamination. Invert tube to make sure the inside of the lid gets sterilised. Let stand for 5 minutes or more, 0.1% NaDCC does not harm the spores so no need to rush.

Collect the spores by centrifugation for 1,5minutes at 13,000 rpm. Most of the spores will now be on the bottom or side of the tube and you can remove some of the sterilisation solution. Do not try to remove it all or you will lose a lot of spores. Wash the spores off the sides of the tube pipetting 500 ul sterile dH2O, and then add the spore suspension to liquid culture.

NOTE: You can use this spore sterilisation method also for any Marchantia spores stored in the -80°C freezer, if you just want to plate the spores you can directly plate them in the sterilisation solution without spinning the spores down. In that case one sporangium is normally plenty!
Sterilisation of spores in intact sporangiums to be used fresh:
Prepare sterilisation solution: 1% NaDCC.
Add 500 ul of sterilisation solution into Eppendorf tube containing 500ul H2O and sporangiums, i.e. strength of the final sterilisation solution is 0.5% NaDCC. Gently invert the tube (do not vortex).
Remove the sterilisation solution (do not leave for longer than few minutes or spores will not germinate!) and rinse three times with 1 ml dH2O.

once the sporangia are sterilized, they can be kept intact in the 3rd 1 ml rinse in the fridge for at least a couple of months, and they still seem to work OK and not have noticeably increased contamination.
NOTE: Do not dry spores sterilised with 0.5% NaDCC. Germination will be reduced and your transformation will not work.

Add 600 ul water and break the sporangiums to release the spores. Avoid taking bits of the sporangiums because this increases chance of getting contamination. Pipette the spore suspension into liquid culture.
Setting up liquid spore cultures
Prepare fresh liquid ½ Gamborgs medium:
0.8g ½ Gamborgs medium powder
10g sucrose (final concentration 2%)
150 mg L-glutamine (final concentration 0.03 %), probably not important but I always added it
Over time the ½ Gamborgs medium turns acidic and then the agrobacterium will not grow in it. I always try to prepare it fresh.

Autoclave the media and let cool. Set up 25 ml cultures in sterile 250 ml Erlenmeyer flasks (cover the top with two layers of foil prior to autoclaving) or 6 ml cultures on sterile 6 well plates (seal with micropore tape). Add spores equivalent to around 1 sterilised sporangium per flask or 0.5-1 sporangium per well.
Grow the spores 6-7 days at 21-23 C constant light at 1500-2000 lux / 80-100 uM in a growth cabinet, not shaking.
Preparation of Agrobacterium
Streak out Agrobacterium carrying your vector on LB containing appropriate antibiotics, or transform your vector in. Grow for two days at 28 °C incubator.
The agrobacterium strain we usually use is GV3101 which has Rif and Gent resistance
MpGWB based Golden Gate vectors (SHp131) and CRISPR transformation vectors (pMpGE011 and pMpGE010) carry spec resistance marker for bacterial selection, use at 100 ug/ml.
T-DNA mutagenesis vector pCambia 1300 carries a Kan resistance marker for bacterial selection, use at 50 ug/ml.
Stock concentrations Final Concentrations:
Spec: 100 mg/ml Spec: 50 ug/ml
Kan: 50 mg/ml Kan: 50 μg/ml
Gent: 25 mg/ml Gent: 25 μg/ml
Rif: 25 mg/ml (in methanol) Rif: 100 μg/ml
Inoculate a single colony of Agrobacterium in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics, grow 1-2 days or overnight at 28 °C shaker.
Centrifuge the bacterial culture for 15 minutes at 2000g.

Pour off the supernatant and add 7 ml (1 day old culture) 10 ml (2 day old culture) of fresh ½ Gamborgs liquid medium containing 100 uM acetosyringone (1:1000 dilution of 100 mM stock in DMSO). Resuspend pellet containing the bacterial cells by shaking the tube.
Induce Agrobacterium by cultivation from 2 (if you are in rush) up to 6 hours at 28 °C 200 rpm on a shaker.

Check that the bacteria does not start to clump. Clumping tends to occur if there were too many cells in the beginning of the induction. If you observe clumping then stop the induction and proceed to add the bacteria to the spore cultures.
Transformation of Marchantia spores with Agrobacterium
Add induced Agrobacterium into 6- or 7-day old liquid culture of liverwort spores, 100 ul (or up to 500 ul if your cultures is thin) to a 6 ml plate well or 1 ml to a 25 ml flask.
Add acetosyringone to final concentration of 100 uM

Co-cultivate for 1-3 days on a 120 rpm shaker (3 days should result in better efficiency based on Ishizaki et al., but if bacteria overgrows the efficiency is actually worse). NOTE: The growth of the bacteria somewhat depends on your construct. I place the plates/flasks in the dark (i.e. cover them with foil), which may improve efficiency, or at least certainly works just fine.
Plating on selective medium
Place a 40 um cell strainer in the opening of a 50 ml falcon tube.

If using a 6 well plate use sterile plastic Pasteur pipette to transfer the spores in media onto the cell strainer. Add distilled water onto the well, scratch off the spores that stick on the well using the same Pasteur pipette and move the dH2O containing remaining spores on the strainer. If using a 25 ml liquid spore culture in a flask slowly pour the culture through the strainer. Hold the strainer above the falcon tube and slightly shake it while pouring the liquid through.
Rinse spores on the filter with at least 50 ml of autoclaved dH2O.

Move the spores from the filter with sterile Pasteur pipette on 1.4% agar plates containing ½ Gamborgs medium with appropriate antibiotics (always 100 ug/ml Cef to kill the agrobacterium, in addition 10ug/ml Hyg or 0.5 uM chlorosulfron to select for transformant plants). NOTE: the agar matters. Cheap agar that has impurities can inhibit transformation. Normally need 3-8 round plates per 25 ml flask or 1-2 plates per 6 ml well. Plate very little spores on some plates and more on others so that can still pick individual transformants even if efficiency was really good (if all plates are too thick hard to separate individual plants). Spread spores using the same sterile plastic Pasteur pipette.
Place in growth chamber (21-23 °C, constant light or 16 hours light 8 hours dark).
Antibiotic resistant transformants should be visible after 1-2 weeks.

When you move the transformants from the selection plate to a new plate you should still add cefotaxime on the new plate; often a bit of agrobacterium remains after the 1-2 week selection and the bacteria will grow again if you do not use antibiotic. After several weeks re-growth of bacteria should no longer be a problem and no antibiotic is needed
